question: Where on the clock curve does the extra time stop paying for the energy saved? Verify the original 1,800 MHz recommendation, in 100 MHz steps down to 1,600.
machine: two-node DGX Spark cluster (2 x GB10), TP2 across both nodes

stack.launch: scripts/launch/dsv41_tp2.sh up, PORT=8888, reasoning_effort low, MAX_SEQS=2 (recipe default)

order: round r starts at arm r (rotation), so each arm takes each position

work_per_run.api: /v1/completions, temperature 0, raw prompt; a per-run nonce first so the prefix cache cannot serve a prompt

cool_down: at least 180 s, then until both GPUs are at or below the idle temperature + 10 C (targets 55 / 53 C), max 900 s. The first A/B used +3 C on an idle measured right after a calibration pass (targets 57 / 58 C).

sensors.gpu: DCGM via Prometheus: SM clock avg/max, GPU temp max, GPU power avg, per node
sensors.fans: head node only (node_exporter hwmon fan1, fan2); the worker has no fan reading
sensors.outlets: Home Assistant smart plugs, one per node, mean and max over the run
sensors.inlet: weather-station indoor sensor at the front of the cluster, last reading at or before the run's end

files.runs.jsonl: one row per run, written by the driver

anchors: uncapped and 1900 repeat the first A/B (benchmarks/clock-cap/1319) inside this session, so every point on the curve shares one session and one room
false_start: 2026-10-31T08:34:28-04:00: the driver measured idle on GPUs still cold from the model load (45 / 42 C, targets 48 / 45 C). It was stopped with SIGINT before any run; its log is driver-aborted-cold-idle.log. The stop restarted gpu-clock-cap.service on both nodes, as designed.
standing_cap: gpu-clock-cap.service (1,900 MHz) is active on both nodes; the driver sets each arm over it and restarts it at the end
